Anatomy of the unmatched 2.4%

2026-08-14, outcome added 2026-08-15 · companion to the matching audit and the QA dashboard · data: the pulse ledger over 272,212 pulses since run_79 (265,693 matched, 97.61 %)

16 August: the last 88 were gone after by brute force, one burst at a time — 25 recovered, 260 re-attributed to n_TOF-not-recording, 34 shown to be stubs and noise; 279,938 / 279,972 = 99.99 %. See the last 88 pulses, one burst at a time. The box below is the 15 August state.

Outcome, 15 August: 277,681 of 277,860 matchable pulses since run_79 are confidently matched — 99.94 %, above the target (at the 60 % per-pulse coincidence bar adopted the same evening, after the per-pulse distribution showed the 70–80 % range to be a smooth tail of one population — 544 pulses, median 73 triggers vs ~82 — rather than a second failure mode; 99.74 % at the old 80 % bar; 99.30 % if in addition the 1,253 pulses n_TOF was not recording are left in the denominator, as this note originally counted them; they are now reported separately as the understood, irrecoverable loss they are — 0.45 % of 279,113 beam pulses — see §3). Every class below resolved the way it was predicted to, with one correction to the diagnosis of the dark hours: they were not a search-window problem but a candidate cap. pulse_match.enumerate_locks handed the coincidence arbiter only the top 8 count-tied candidates (_lock_records' default limit, meant for the cached diagnostic record). The true locks — +62.72 s, +59.12 s, +26.54 s, each exactly the count-scan's baseline plus 172.8 s = four supercycles — were the 9th-or-later ties and were never measured. With every candidate offered (commit 0c18f31) the arbiter accepted them at 95–97 % on the first or second try: run_116/0027 → 94.2 %, run_118/0017 → 94.1 / 93.7 % on 224646/224647 (the same +59.12 s lock on both; the −131-bunch wide-scan verdict on 224647 was an alias), run_122/0000 → 94.0 %. The five never-attempted segments ran (run_162/0010 95.5 %, run_147/0003 96.3 %, run_154/0003 96.5 %). And the ledger's 53 "lock-pending" sub-runs turned out to hide ~7,000 pulses in whole hours whose 12 Aug slim jobs had died on scratch disk at their second segment (run_116/0026, run_147/0001–2, run_154/0001–2, run_162/0008–9): all now slimmed at 94–97 %, and inside the denominator. What remains outside it: run_161's 25 HV-scan sub-runs on n_TOF 224709 (~2,200 pulses; the run is 206 GB and is being read off EOS without staging), run_120/0000 (272, no n_TOF run proposed) and 19 single-burst calibration modes. Live numbers: the match QA page.

The 13 August analysis, as written

Of the 6,519 pulses not confidently matched, roughly 4,600 are plausibly recoverable by two concrete actions, ~1,400 are structurally unmatchable (n_TOF was not recording), and 523 are matched in all but name. If the recoverable classes recover, the headline reaches ~99.3 % — above the 99 % target. The two actions: a wide bunch-shift scan on each of three anomalous hours (3,680 pulses), and proposing five segments that were simply never run (928 pulses).

§1 The three dark hours — 3,680 pulses, the big recoverable block

Three full hour-long sub-runs where every enumerated candidate lock was measured by the coincidence and every one scored 0.00 %. These are not ambiguous refusals; the instrument looked and said no — but only at the candidates it was offered. Everything else about these hours is measured normal:

  • DREAM is normal: burst multiplicity is identical to healthy neighbours (median 82–83 triggers/burst, same 70/82/106 percentiles in the failed hour and its siblings), burst counts are full (1,178–1,251), and the filename anchors step in perfect hourly continuity through the failed hours.
  • n_TOF is normal: the same n_TOF runs are matched at full rate by neighbouring sub-runs — 224640 by run_116/0028 (1,066 pulses), 224646/47 by run_118/0015–0020 (~1,200 each), 224652 by run_124/0000–0002.
  • run_118/stat090_0017 is the sharpest case: it sits between 0016 (matches 224646) and 0018 (matches 224647), straddles the run boundary as its wall-clock says it should, was tried against both runs — and scored 0 % on every candidate against both.

[15 Aug: right conclusion, wrong mechanism — the true lock was inside ±120 s and inside the enumeration; it was cut by a top-8 cap before the arbiter saw it. See the outcome box above.]

The one hypothesis left standing: the true lock is not among the enumerated candidates — the same supercycle-alias family as the 8-12 mislocks, one step worse: instead of a wrong in-window candidate silently winning, no in-window candidate is right, which the new chain correctly refuses rather than guesses. The discriminating instrument already exists and has precedent: segment_diagnose --span 200 found exactly one sharp peak (S/N 541–1822) in 8 of 8 previously scanned failures. Action: three wide scans. If a peak appears, re-issue with accept_offset_s and the standard chain recovers the hour; if the scan is flat, these hours are genuinely dark and move to the structural column (ceiling then ~98.0 %).

§2 Never attempted — 928 pulses, the free ones

Bursts inside an n_TOF run's recorded span for which no segment was ever proposed. Five pairs, three of them material:

run_162×224714 is the end of data taking (last beam run 224715), which is likely why the coverage proposal stopped short. Action: propose and slim five segments — the coincidence-first chain decides the locks automatically now, so these cost one condor pass.

§3 n_TOF not recording — 1,235 pulses, the structural floor

1,204 pulses fall in inter-run transitions — the PS kept delivering while the n_TOF DAQ cycled between runs. The typical gap is 0.5–1.7 minutes (run-restart dead time, ~4 pulses each, scattered across the whole campaign); the single largest is a 25.5-minute hole between 224621 and 224622 (65 pulses). The remaining 31 are in-run PKUP holes, verified per-pulse against the production PKUP tables. Beam we took that n_TOF did not record is not recoverable by any processing; this class is the honest floor under the headline, and excluding it is what the 98.05 % number means.

§4 Low coincidence — 523 pulses, matched in all but name

These pulses joined to the right bunch (their sub-runs' locks are coincidence-verified); they simply have 73–80 % of their triggers coincident against the 80 % bar (median 78 %, p10 73 %). They are spread across 216 sub-runs at ≤8 pulses each — no pathological block — and they are systematically smaller bursts (median 74 triggers vs 96 for matched pulses), i.e. the statistical tail of single-leg detector inefficiency against a hard threshold, not a matching failure. The leg breakdown is the same as the campaign-wide one (wall-absent : plastic-absent ≈ 1:1 here, neither only 9 of 523). No action needed: for physics these joins are usable as-is; the 80 % bar is a purity choice with the two populations at 96 % and 0.00 %, and nothing sits below it but this tail.

§5 The residue — ~153 pulses, individually explained

  • No-overlap slivers (65): tails of run_108/0000, run_112/0000, run_126/0000 outside any n_TOF run's data — the δ-scan now refuses these by name ("nothing to lock onto in the band"), confirmed against synthetic no-overlap trains. No partner data exists.
  • run_82/stat090_h2i5_0007 (39): all three candidates measured at 0 % — small enough that a wide scan is optional; same treatment as §1 if ever wanted.
  • run_137/stat090_0000 (19) and run_110/stat090_0003 (21): DAQ stubs — 19–21 bursts with median 3 triggers, nothing to lock onto (run_137 is on the historically dark-run list).
  • Single-burst calibration blocks (~8): clamp/mpack sub-runs of exactly one burst each; NoLock by construction.

What this does not settle

  • Whether the three dark hours actually recover — the wide scans decide, and both outcomes are stated above with their resulting ceilings (~99.3 % vs ~98.0 %).
  • 53 sub-runs remain outside the denominator entirely: 19 calibration trigger modes with no product ('no product, never measured' — decidable only from the DAQ-side N1081B configs), and ~34 stat090 sub-runs awaiting censuses or products. They are listed on the dashboard, not hidden.
  • The trigger-level inefficiency (the 4 % of triggers inside matched pulses missing one scintillator leg, 52 % wall-absent / 38 % plastic-absent) is a detector question, not a matching one — now measurable per-pulse and per-arm from the ledger arrays if it becomes worth chasing.
